analysis: Integration review of the SSD read single-copy change. The only production change is SSDBlockStore.readExactly (patch hunk @@ -481,7 +481,6, head ~481-505). It removes the up-front reserveCapacity(count) and adds a fast path: if the first read returns exactly `count` bytes with startIndex == 0, that Data is returned uncopied. Otherwise it reserves capacity and appends as before. The loop, the beforeRead(count) then beforeRead(0) charging sequence, and the truncated-on-EOF error are unchanged. Return semantics (exactly `count` bytes or a throw) are preserved. Deferring the reservation does not enlarge any allocation. The unauthenticated-length allocation caps in readHeader (per the unit 2 analysis) are unaffected. No change to AES-GCM/AAD, HKDF nonces, DBK3 format, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, no-follow IO or path safety, so the T-041 posture is unchanged. The uncopied buffer is only a lower-memory alias of the read result; the startIndex == 0 guard protects zero-based callers. The new test (SSDBlockStreamingTests.swift lines 259-283) pins the charge sequences [span,0] and [span,0,0] for whole and short reads, and uses a temporary fixture with synthetic bytes. The docs and changelog edits accurately describe the change and alter no controls. Residual unverified points are outside the supplied evidence: other readExactly callers (readStreaming, SSDBlockChunkCursor), and whether the underlying read helper can return more than `count` bytes. The oversize case falls through to append, which is the pre-existing behavior. These are low-risk and no concrete regression is supported.
